```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with get-started and the tour:
# the source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a
# bare installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# This page runs against committed test bytes only: the SigProfiler specimen
# fixture under tests/testthat/fixtures/, plus small objects built in memory
# with ms_simulate(). No downloads, no real data -- the claims-are-measured
# law of the docs/site lanes.
FIX <- local({
  if (is.na(PKG)) stop("the io fixtures require the source checkout")
  fp <- file.path(PKG, "tests", "testthat", "fixtures",
                  "sigprofiler_sbs96_specimen.txt")
  if (!file.exists(fp)) stop("specimen fixture missing: ", fp)
  fp
})
```

## One door for every external format

The io layer is the only part of msuiter that touches external formats. Each
entry point dispatches on its first argument: a file path is read and repaired
at load time (column mapping, coordinate parsing, a skip ledger that counts
every dropped record into provenance), while a canonical data.frame skips the
reading and goes straight to validation. Every violation raises an
`msuiter_error_*` condition that names the field, the expectation and the fix.

## Variant records: `ms_variants()`

The canonical record is a data.frame with columns `chrom`, `start`, `end`,
`ref` and `alt`, plus optional `vaf` and `filter`. Alleles are uppercase
`A/C/G/T/N` strings of any length, so single-base substitutions, equal-length
multi-base events and length-changing events all ride the same table; routing
into the channel-specific tallies happens downstream, at the catalog layer.
Coordinates are 1-based and closed (`start >= 1`, `end >= start`). Three
provenance arguments are required -- `genome`, `caller` and `matched_normal`
(use `"none"` for tumor-only calls); `vaf_floor` is optional.

```{r variants-df}
tab <- data.frame(
  chrom  = c("chr1", "chr1", "chr7",    "chr17"),
  start  = c(12L,    22L,    55191822L, 7676594L),
  end    = c(12L,    23L,    55191822L, 7676595L),
  ref    = c("C",    "CA",   "C",       "CA"),
  alt    = c("A",    "TT",   "T",       "C"),
  vaf    = c(0.62,   0.55,   0.71,      0.48),
  filter = c("PASS", "PASS", "PASS",    ".")
)
v <- ms_variants(tab, genome = "GRCh38", caller = "synthetic",
                 matched_normal = "none", vaf_floor = 0.05)
v
v@table
```

The double-base row (`CA` -> `TT`) and the length-changing row (`CA` -> `C`)
validate through the same constructor as the SNV row; the optional `vaf` and
`filter` columns pass through untouched into provenance and the typed table.

File input works the same way for VCF, TSV and MAF (optionally
gzip-compressed). Writing VCF-like records to a tempfile shows the reading
face, including the multiallelic expansion and the skip ledger:

```{r variants-vcf}
lines <- c(
  "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
  "#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO",
  "chr7\t55191822\t.\tC\tT\t.\tPASS\t.",
  "chr1\t22\t.\tCA\tTT,G\t.\t.\t.",
  "chr1\t30\t.\tC\t<NON_REF>\t.\t.\t."
)
vcf_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf")
writeLines(lines, vcf_path)
v2 <- ms_variants(vcf_path, "GRCh38", caller = "demo-caller",
                  matched_normal = "none")
v2@table
v2@provenance$parse
unlink(vcf_path)
```

The multi-allelic site expands to a record per ALT allele, the symbolic
`<NON_REF>` allele lands in `skip_reasons` (never silently dropped), and
`end` is derived as `pos + nchar(ref) - 1` where the source carries no end
coordinate. TSV and MAF files are remapped with
`chrom_col`/`pos_col`/`end_col`/`ref_col`/`alt_col` (TSV defaults to
`chrom/pos/ref/alt`, MAF to the standard GDC-style names), with `filter_col`
and `vaf_col` as optional passthroughs, and `format` forces the reader when
the extension is not decisive. BCF is rejected with an actionable message,
and so is any stray argument in `...` -- the io functions have no passthrough.

## Segments and rearrangements: `ms_segments()` and `ms_sv()`

Copy-number segments and structural variants enter through the same dispatch.
The canonical segment record is `chrom`/`start`/`end` plus the ordered
allele-specific pair `minor`/`major` (the total copy number is their sum). On
the file path the caller's columns are mapped for the
SigProfilerMatrixGenerator copy-number callers (ASCAT, ASCAT_NGS, ABSOLUTE,
PCAWG, FACETS, BATTENBERG, PURPLE, SEQUENZA), auto-detected from the column
signature with `caller = "auto"`; a canonical data.frame carries no
per-caller columns, so an explicit `caller` label is required there.

```{r segments-sv}
seg <- ms_segments(
  data.frame(chrom = "chr7", start = 100000L, end = 9000000L,
             minor = 1L, major = 1L),
  caller = "ASCAT"
)
seg

sv <- ms_sv(data.frame(
  chrom1 = "19", start1 = 21268384L, end1 = 21268385L,
  chrom2 = "19", start2 = 21327858L, end2 = 21327859L,
  strand1 = "+", strand2 = "+"
))
sv[, c("svtype", "size_bp", "clustered")]
```

`ms_sv()` takes BEDPE -- the six coordinate columns plus either an `svclass`
column or the `strand1`/`strand2` pair -- and derives the rearrangement
class, the event size and the kat-region `clustered` flag like the upstream
SigProfilerMatrixGenerator implementation. Both functions return typed
data.frames with the reading provenance in attribute `"provenance"`.

## Catalog and signature files: `ms_export()` and `ms_import()`

The catalog face interchanges channel x column matrices in the verified
layouts: `cosmic` (first header column `Type`) and `sigprofiler` (first
header column `MutationType`). Import resolves the channel table by exact
label-set match against the registry -- no silent reordering, no silent
subsets -- or you pin it with `channel_table`.

```{r import-specimen}
sig <- ms_import(FIX, format = "sigprofiler", kind = "signatures")
sig
c(channel = sig@catalog_summary$channel_name,
  build   = strtrim(sig@catalog_summary$build, 24L))
```

`kind = "catalog"` expects finite non-negative whole numbers and returns an
`MsCatalog`; `kind = "signatures"` reads the columns as probabilities and
returns an `MsSignature` with the legal zero-column exposure face, its
catalog summary recording the file's sha256 digest.

### A round trip through both layouts

Export accepts either an `MsCatalog` (the counts, a column per sample) or an
`MsSignature` (the signature probabilities); `file = NULL` returns the
assembled data.frame instead of writing. The specimen imported above feeds a
simulated catalog, and both objects then go out and come back through their
respective layouts:

```{r roundtrip-setup}
ex <- matrix(rep(0.1, ncol(sig@signatures)), ncol = 1L)
cat1 <- ms_simulate(sig, ex, burden = 400, seed = 7)
cat1
head(ms_export(cat1, format = "cosmic"), 2L)
```

```{r roundtrip-files}
cosmic_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
ms_export(cat1, format = "cosmic", file = cosmic_file)
cat2 <- ms_import(cosmic_file, format = "cosmic", kind = "catalog")
max(abs(cat2@counts - cat1@counts))   # integer counts survive verbatim

sp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
ms_export(sig, format = "sigprofiler", file = sp_file)
sig2 <- ms_import(sp_file, format = "sigprofiler", kind = "signatures")
max(abs(sig2@signatures - sig@signatures))
file.remove(c(cosmic_file, sp_file))
```

The count matrix comes back unchanged; the probability matrix carries only
floating-point dust from the decimal serialisation.

## Opportunity conversion: `ms_convert()`

Signatures fitted genome-wide and signatures fitted on exomes sit on
different trinucleotide opportunity baselines. `ms_convert()` re-expresses an
SBS96 signature set between opportunity vectors with the sigfit
`convert_signatures` semantics: divide by the source opportunities, multiply
by the target ones, re-normalize each column. The bundled tables are
`"human-genome"` and `"human-exome"`; a custom named frequency vector is
accepted for panel targets.

```{r convert}
exome <- ms_convert(sig, from = "human-genome", to = "human-exome")
exome
colSums(exome@signatures)[1L:3L]
```

The `MsSignature` method returns a new object with the converted
`signatures` slot and the exposures untouched -- exposure shares are
opportunity-agnostic under this semantics. Converting back recovers the
genome-scale profile:

```{r convert-back}
back <- ms_convert(exome, from = "human-exome", to = "human-genome")
max(abs(back@signatures - sig@signatures))  # floating-point residue only
identical(dim(exome@exposures), dim(sig@exposures))
```

A plain numeric matrix works too, provided it carries the SBS96 registry
rownames in canonical order -- the opportunity values are matched by label,
never by position:

```{r convert-matrix}
m <- ms_convert(sig@signatures, "human-genome", "human-exome")
identical(dim(m), dim(sig@signatures))
```
